title: Green Bean Casserole
subtitle: tender green beans in a from-scratch creamy sauce under crispy onions
imageAlt: A baking dish of green bean casserole in a creamy sauce topped with golden crispy onions, a serving on a cream plate beside a navy napkin

beforeYouStart.text: Blanch the beans just until bright and crisp-tender; they finish in the oven.
Save half the crispy onions for the end so they stay crunchy.

items.name: green beans
items.note: trimmed and cut in 5 cm pieces

steps.title: Blanch
steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Boil the beans in salted water 5 minutes, drain and rinse under cold water.

steps.title: Sauce
steps.text: Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium. Cook the onion 4 minutes until soft, add the garlic 30 seconds, then stir in the flour for 1 minute. Whisk in the broth and milk and simmer 3–4 minutes until thick. Stir in the soy sauce, Parmesan, salt and pepper.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Fold the beans and half the crispy onions into the sauce and spread in a 2 L baking dish.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 20 minutes until bubbling, scatter the rest of the onions on top and bake 5 minutes more.

fixIt.fix: Loosen with a splash of milk before adding the beans.
Add the top layer only for the last 5 minutes.
Rinse them cold right after blanching to keep them bright.

saleTip: Frozen cut green beans work well here and are often cheaper than fresh in the fall.
swap: Frozen green beans (skip blanching, thaw and pat dry). Cheddar for Parmesan.
leftovers: Best fresh; leftovers lose their crunch but taste good.
doneness: Bake until bubbling at the edges and hot in the centre, 74°C (165°F) when reheating (Health Canada).
source: Based on tested from-scratch green bean casserole methods (Serious Eats, Canadian Living): blanched beans in a roux-thickened broth and milk sauce, topped with crispy fried onions. Made without the classic canned soup.
prepAhead: Make the sauce and blanch the beans a day ahead; combine and bake with 10 extra minutes.
reheat: Covered at 175°C (350°F) for 15 minutes, or in the microwave, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Beans in a simple cream sauce with crispy onions; no Parmesan or soy sauce.

stepNotes.1: Basic: skip the soy sauce and Parmesan.

fancy.note: Gruyère melted through the sauce and crisp bacon on top.

stepNotes.1: Fancy: cook the bacon in the skillet first, crumble it, then make the sauce and stir in the Gruyère with the Parmesan.
stepNotes.3: Fancy: scatter the bacon with the last onions.

plating: A golden onion crust on top.

why.2-0: Half inside for flavour, half on top for crunch.
why.1-6: A teaspoon of soy sauce adds the savoury depth canned soup used to give.

funFact: Green bean casserole was created in 1955 in the Campbell's test kitchen by Dorcas Reilly.

keeps.note: the cream sauce and onions go soggy
